correctness.rationale: On X=P^a×P^b over C, A^a B^b=1 and (A+B)^(a+b) gives Chow degree C=binom(d,a). Adjunction with K=−(a+1)A−(b+1)B computes sectional genus of a generic complete-intersection curve; the smooth-variety Hurwitz theorem H=2C+2g−2 simplifies to H=(2ab/d)C=2(d−1)!/((a−1)!(b−1)!). With reduced multiplier numerator u/denominator q, q=d/gcd(d,2ab) divides C because H integer, so gcd(C,H)=C/q. If a=1, gcd(b+1,2b)=gcd(b+1,2), yielding coprime iff b even; if both a,b≥2, C≥binom(d,2)>d≥q hence gcd>1. Independently checked 40,000 pairs a,b=1..200 with exact Python integers. The symbolic geometric and arithmetic proofs, not regression, cover all dimensions.

value.rationale: Consecutive associated-hypersurface degrees form a canonical sequence in projective geometry, and their gcd/coprimality is a natural arithmetic integrality comparison—not an arbitrary parameter slice. The complete infinite two-parameter coprimality classification (exactly P¹×P^{even} up to swap), including proof that all higher-factor dimensions obstruct it, is a usable exact structural fact. It is short once Sturmfels and Segre intersection ring are combined, and its scientific value is modest but meets the bar for an exact natural previously unlocated invariant without demanding a general new geometric theorem.
residual_risks: A reader may regard this as immediate once both degree formulas are known; no claimed downstream theorem or major innovation.

final_claim: For complex Segre X=P^a×P^b (a,b≥1), Chow degree C=binom(a+b,a) and Hurwitz degree H=(2ab/(a+b))C satisfy gcd(C,H)=C·gcd(a+b,2ab)/(a+b); they are coprime exactly for (a,b)=(1,2m) or (2m,1), m≥1.
limitations: Only smooth standard complex Segre embedding O(1,1), not Segre-Veronese, higher polar sequences or singular varieties.
Input geometric degree theorem is known; contribution is limited arithmetic comparison with acknowledged prior-overlap risk.
